card.intuition: Carries information forward. A session is stateful across turns — context accumulates as it runs, which is why long sessions drift into the dumb zone. An agent can be made stateful across sessions by adding a memory system that persists information into the environment and reloads it at the start of future sessions. The model itself is never stateful; any apparent continuity is the harness re-feeding context.
card.analogy: A project notebook your assistant reloads every morning: yesterday's decisions get written down and re-read, so it picks up where it left off even though its recollection is just re-reading the notebook, not memory.
card.time_complexity: The model re-reads the entire context on every turn, so cost and latency grow with context size per request.
card.space_complexity: State is stored by re-reading something at a lower layer: files and transcripts consume context-window budget or disk, and each reload re-competes for window space.
when_to_use: Adding a memory system so an agent remembers preferences or decisions across sessions
Relying on handoff artifacts and AGENTS.md to carry state between sessions
Accepting that within a session, accumulated context is what keeps the agent coherent
gotchas: A wrong assumption made early is carried forward and influences every later turn — clearing is the deliberate reset
The model saw nothing of yesterday; apparent continuity is the harness reloading storage, never the model remembering

exercise.prompt: Simulate a memory system: append a note for the session and return a snapshot that a future session could reload.
hints: Each session should get its own snapshot copy, not the live list.
Slice the whole list to return a fresh copy.
exercise.test_code:
mem = ["known: repo is a monorepo"]
out = reload_memory(mem, "note: use pnpm")
assert out == ["known: repo is a monorepo", "note: use pnpm"]
assert len(out) == 2
assert out is not mem
print('PASS')
